_comment: Every data-bearing field in every seed record names one of these sources by
id, and the loader materialises the full record onto the field, so what a
consumer sees is a fully-resolved ProvenanceRecord per field — not a pointer.
The registry exists because the alternative, copying an identical 11-key
object next to ~200 fields by hand, drifts. Drifted provenance is worse than
no provenance: it is provenance that lies.
A field may override only confidence, review_status, source_entry_id and
notes. source, source_version, license, attribution and modification_status
are NOT overridable, so no field can quietly relicense itself.
test/provenance.test.ts enforces both halves of that.

kanjivg-verbatim.notes: Byte-identical copies of the upstream SVG files, including their in-file copyright header. Per-file URL and sha256 are in data/strokes.json; test/strokes.test.ts re-checks the digests offline and scripts/fetch-kanjivg.mjs --check re-checks them against upstream.

kanjivg-derived.attribution: Derived from KanjiVG, copyright Ulrich Apel, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/ — see https://kanjivg.tagaini.net and packages/seed/licenses/KanjiVG-COPYING.txt
kanjivg-derived.notes: Stroke counts and component/radical decompositions read out of the committed KanjiVG SVGs (kvg:element, kvg:radical, kvg:*-sN path ids). Share-alike analysis of a CC BY-SA 3.0 work; test/strokes.test.ts re-derives every value from the SVG bytes, so these fields cannot drift away from their source.

edrdg-jmdict.source_version: JMdict_e (English edition), retrieved from www.edrdg.org on 2026-07-28; 218,148 entries
edrdg-jmdict.attribution: This product uses the JMdict dictionary file. JMdict is the property of the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, copyright James William BREEN and the EDRDG, and is used in conformance with the Group's licence: https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project — licence statement verbatim in packages/seed/licenses/EDRDG-licence-statement.html, full legal code in packages/seed/licenses/CC-BY-SA-4.0.html
edrdg-jmdict.notes: Real JMdict entries; each field's source_entry_id is that entry's real ent_seq. modification_status is derived, not unmodified, for one specific reason: the seed schema stores senses and parts of speech as flat string lists, so upstream sense boundaries are lost by the shape. reading is the entry's first kana element; partOfSpeech and senses are every value across every sense in upstream order, deduplicated. Retrieved directly from the licensor's host, so this is primary-source-verified rather than licensed-redistribution: the previous round could only reach a redistribution and its bundled licence copy said CC BY-SA 3.0, which the licensor's own statement contradicts — the licence is 4.0. Every committed value was re-derived from the file named in source_url and re-checked field by field with scripts/import-sources.mjs --verify-fixtures.

edrdg-kanjidic2.source_version: KANJIDIC2, retrieved from www.edrdg.org on 2026-07-28; 13,108 characters
edrdg-kanjidic2.attribution: This product uses the KANJIDIC2 dictionary file. KANJIDIC2 is the property of the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, copyright James William BREEN and the EDRDG, and is used in conformance with the Group's licence: https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/KANJIDIC_Project — licence statement verbatim in packages/seed/licenses/EDRDG-licence-statement.html, full legal code in packages/seed/licenses/CC-BY-SA-4.0.html
edrdg-kanjidic2.notes: Real KANJIDIC2 characters; source_entry_id is the literal, which is KANJIDIC2's own entry identifier. onReadings and kunReadings are the ja_on and ja_kun readings in upstream order; meanings are the English <meaning> elements only. strokeCount is NOT taken from here — the seed derives it from the KanjiVG file it ships, and KANJIDIC2's stroke_count agreeing on all ten characters is an independent cross-check that would be destroyed by copying one into the other. Retrieved directly from the licensor's host, so this is primary-source-verified rather than licensed-redistribution: the previous round could only reach a redistribution and its bundled licence copy said CC BY-SA 3.0, which the licensor's own statement contradicts — the licence is 4.0. Every committed value was re-derived from the file named in source_url and re-checked field by field with scripts/import-sources.mjs --verify-fixtures.

bunki-editorial.source: Bunki Phase-0 seed (hand-assembled by this project)
bunki-editorial.license: pending operator decision (OD-09) — original work of this project, no third-party licence attaches
bunki-editorial.notes: Lexicographic claims written from the builder's own knowledge of Japanese, retained only where no licensed source replaced them. The lexeme readings/senses/parts of speech and the kanji on/kun readings and meanings that this source used to cover are now real JMdict and KANJIDIC2 entries (see edrdg-jmdict, edrdg-kanjidic2). What is left under this source is labelled unreviewed and carries no entry identifier, because there is none to carry.

bunki-authored-text.source: Bunki Phase-0 seed (original text written for this project)
bunki-authored-text.license: pending operator decision (OD-09) — original work of this project, no third-party licence attaches
bunki-authored-text.attribution: Bunki Phase-0 seed dataset — original text
bunki-authored-text.notes: Japanese sentences, the integration passage, and grammar explanations composed for this project. Not sourced from Tatoeba or any corpus: Tatoeba's hosts were unreachable from this build session (LICENSES.md, deferred item D-2), and inventing sentence ids or contributor names would have been fabrication. These are original compositions and carry no third-party attribution obligation.

bunki-selection.source: Bunki Phase-0 seed (selection decision by this project)
bunki-selection.license: pending operator decision (OD-09) — original work of this project, no third-party licence attaches
bunki-selection.notes: Fields that record a choice rather than a claim: which kanji and headwords the seed covers, which construction a sentence illustrates, which records the integration passage is wired to. The glyphs themselves are Unicode characters, not licensed assets; nothing here asserts anything a dictionary could contradict.

bunki-computed.license: pending operator decision (OD-09) — original work of this project, no third-party licence attaches
bunki-computed.notes: Values a machine derives from the field's own subject — a Unicode code point from its character, the kanji used by a headword from the headword string. The test suite recomputes each one and fails on any mismatch, so these are the only seed fields that are self-verifying.

tatoeba-japanese.source_version: jpn_sentences_detailed.tsv, retrieved from downloads.tatoeba.org on 2026-07-28; 248,821 Japanese sentences
tatoeba-japanese.attribution: Sentence from the Tatoeba Project (https://tatoeba.org), used under CC BY 2.0 FR: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/fr/ — full legal code in packages/seed/licenses/CC-BY-2.0-FR.html. The contributing member is named per sentence in the record, because this licence attributes the individual author, not the corpus.
tatoeba-japanese.notes: Sentence text verbatim, never edited. The per-record tatoeba.japaneseId is the real Tatoeba sentence id and japaneseContributor the real contributing username; a sentence whose contributor could not be resolved was not shipped, because an attribution licence with no attributable author cannot be complied with.

tatoeba-english.source_version: eng_sentences_detailed.tsv + links.csv, retrieved from downloads.tatoeba.org on 2026-07-28
tatoeba-english.attribution: English translation from the Tatoeba Project (https://tatoeba.org), used under CC BY 2.0 FR: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/fr/ — full legal code in packages/seed/licenses/CC-BY-2.0-FR.html. The contributing member is named per sentence in the record.
tatoeba-english.notes: The English half of a Tatoeba pair is a separate work by a separate contributor, linked through the project's own links export. It carries its own id and its own credit rather than inheriting the Japanese sentence's, because collapsing the two would misattribute both.
